text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: high 5xx rate on dedicated-us-west-2-03 affecting tenant=MaplePay. Initial spike ~2812345600-2812345660. Alert: 502/504 and connection resets. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/maplepay-errors

sarah-nguyen: I’m on it. Gonna check cluster metrics + logs. Anyone seeing KV eviction spikes?

mike-choi: I see a sharp rise in per-GPU CPU utilization on pool gpu-pool-03 and KV evictions + tail latency. Likely noisy neighbor causing paging.

javier-ops: Confirmed. KV eviction rate up 18x since 10m ago. Network egress looks normal. Dedicated autoscaler didn’t kick — pool shows pinned min nodes.

sarah-nguyen: Customer impact? How many requests failing?

amy-cs: Customer reported timeouts in support ticket #MP-431. They say ~40% of requests failing for last 12 minutes.

mike-choi: From our side error-rate for tenant MaplePay = 41% 5xx in the last 5m, total qps for tenant ~120 rps. Overall cluster error-rate elevated but concentrated on that dedicated tenant.

robin-eng: If it's noisy neighbor on same pool we can: 1) throttle offending tenant, 2) evict to another node (if allowed), 3) route MaplePay to cold fallback variant. Which path first?

sarah-nguyen: Throttle is fastest. Apply temporary rate cap for MaplePay to reduce KV churn, set to 60rps. Also open canary route to fallback model-small-latency for their requests.

incident-bot: Executing runbook step: applying quota -> POST /admin/tenants/MaplePay/quota {max_rps:60} (dry-run false)

mike-choi: Quota applied, confirmed by admin API. Sending annotation to console.

javier-ops: Kicked off node drain for node gpu-03-12 that shows high swap/paging. Drain in progress — 1 node at a time.

sarah-nguyen: Also toggled sticky-routing to prefer other pools in us-west-2 while drain finishes.

robin-eng: Opened fallback route: maplepay -> model:open-small-latency v1 (best-effort). This will lower quality slightly but should stabilize latency and reduce KV usage.

amy-cs: I told customer we’re throttling to reduce errors and will follow up in 30m. They asked for ETA.

sarah-nguyen: ETA 30m for stabilization, will update if any change.

runtime-service: Adding note: observed per-request KV lookup latency rose from 2ms to 78ms correlated with eviction spikes. Batching behavior exacerbated under backpressure.

mike-choi: Running quick tail of gateway logs for MaplePay:
```
[2026-03-15T10:45:12Z] tenant=MaplePay path=/generate status=502 backend=runtime error="kv_get_timeout" latency=452ms
[2026-03-15T10:45:13Z] tenant=MaplePay path=/generate status=504 backend=gateway error="upstream_timeout"
[2026-03-15T10:45:14Z] tenant=OtherTenant path=/generate status=200
```

sarah-nguyen: Good signal. KV timeouts causing 502/504. Mitigation so far: quota + fallback routing + node drain. Any immediate need to scale up pool? Autoscaler disabled, we can increase reserved nodes manually.

javier-ops: We can add 2 nodes from reserve in us-west-2. Manual add takes ~4 minutes to come up. If throttling and fallback not enough in 5m we should add nodes.

robin-eng: Also recommend enabling ephemeral cache warming for MaplePay’s hot prefixes to reduce KV load: run a small synthetic warm request set (from ops) hitting top prefixes.

mike-choi: Doing warmup script now (small sampling).

incident-bot: Update: MaplePay error-rate dropped from 41% -> 18% after quota + fallback (1m after change). Monitoring: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/maplepay-errors?orgId=1

amy-cs: Customer acknowledging errors improving but still seeing intermittent failures. They want postmortem and timeline.

sarah-nguyen: We’ll keep QoS in place until pool normalized. Javier, proceed to add 2 reserve nodes if error-rate stays >10% after 10m.

javier-ops: Adding nodes now. Request submitted to infra API (req id 0x7f3a). Expected ready ~4m.

mike-choi: While nodes come up, I’m going to reduce batch sizes for MaplePay to limit concurrency pressure: set batch.max_tokens=512 batch.max_concurrency=8 for tenant route.

robin-eng: Applied batch config. Also set fallback TTL so users routed back to primary once health checks pass.

incident-bot: Manual handoff requested by sarah-nguyen to mike-choi for the next 30m.

sarah-nguyen: Handing to Mike; I need to hop to on-call coordination call. Mike you own updates and customer comms now. :thumbsup:

mike-choi: Acknowledged. Will post status every 10m or on notable changes.

amy-cs: I relayed to the customer that we applied throttling and additional nodes are coming. They asked for an ETA on full restore — I gave 30-45m.

runtime-service: New nodes healthy and joined pool. KV eviction rate down 70% and per-request KV latency back to ~3-5ms.

incident-bot: Metrics snapshot: MaplePay 5xx now 6% (was 41%), p95 latency down 45%. Nodes added: 2. Actions so far: quota throttle, fallback routing, batch tuning, node drain, manual scale, cache warm.

mike-choi: Marking incident as mitigated for paging/noisy-neighbor. Will keep monitoring for 1h and then remove temporary throttles and fallback gradually. Creating follow-up tickets:
- INC-2812345678-A: Investigate why autoscaler didn't react for dedicated pool (owner: eng-infra)
- INC-2812345678-B: Postmortem and customer comms draft (owner: product/ops)
- INC-2812345678-C: Consider tenant isolation improvements (owner: runtime)

amy-cs: Customer updated: they see improvements, appreciate the quick action. Asking for root cause and what prevents recurrence.

sarah-nguyen: On-call notes: avoid blanket min-pinned nodes for high-variance tenants, improve KV backpressure handling, and ensure autoscaler has override to react to eviction signals.

robin-eng: Will follow up with a short RCA doc and link to postmortem ticket.

mike-choi: Closing thread for live mitigation. Will post final incident summary after postmortem. If anyone else has logs or signals to attach, paste here.

incident-bot: Incident severity -> SEV-3 (customer-impacting, degraded for single dedicated tenant). Logged timeline and actions.
